description: Stable Sparse RRT (SST) plans for systems that you can only simulate forward: you apply a control for some time and see where the system goes. Each step selects the cheapest *active* node near a random sample, applies a random control for a random duration, and checks every integration step for collisions. SST keeps the new node only if it is the cheapest node near its *witness*, a point that stands for a small ball of radius `δ_s`; the node it beats becomes inactive, and SST deletes inactive leaves, so the tree stays sparse. SST needs no steering function, and it is *asymptotically near-optimal*: with more iterations, the chance to find a path within a bounded factor of the optimal cost goes to one.

papers.authors: Yanbo Li, Zakary Littlefield, Kostas E. Bekris
papers.title: Asymptotically optimal sampling-based kinodynamic planning
papers.venue: The International Journal of Robotics Research
